div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 15px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #00294D;
display: inline-block; font-size: 22px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #00294D; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: Where a streamed response can be stopped, and where it cannot

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 42px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 13px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: Input guardrails run before the first chunk and can kill the request. Output guardrails run after the last one and cannot. The asymmetry is the whole point of the diagram.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 105px; margin-left: 23px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;

div.div: ONE STREAMING REQUEST, LEFT TO RIGHT

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 180px; height: 1px; padding-top: 143px; margin-left: 33px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: The app sends stream: true in the request body. The gateway answers with server-sent events over the same HTTPS connection.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 180px; height: 1px; padding-top: 143px; margin-left: 269px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Before-request hooks are evaluated before the stream starts, while the gateway still owns the whole response.

This one enforces
Needs async = false. Then deny = true returns 446 and nothing reaches the provider; deny = false returns 246 and the call continues.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 180px; height: 1px; padding-top: 143px; margin-left: 505px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: The gateway swaps in the provider credential and opens its own stream upstream. The provider begins emitting tokens.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 180px; height: 1px; padding-top: 143px; margin-left: 741px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: Each frame is passed to the client as it arrives, and the gateway keeps a copy so it can assemble the response later.

Point of no return
Text delivered here is already on the client. Nothing downstream can take it back.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 180px; height: 1px; padding-top: 143px; margin-left: 977px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: The provider sends the final [DONE] chunk. The gateway parses the accumulated chunks into one complete response.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 180px; height: 1px; padding-top: 143px; margin-left: 1213px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span: After-request hooks run on that assembled response, and their verdicts are sent as one extra chunk after [DONE].

This one only reports
No action is taken. Fallback does not fire, retry does not fire, and the client already has the text.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 410px; height: 1px; padding-top: 358px; margin-left: 273px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Blocked here — the request is rejected before a single token is generated, the app gets 446, and the attempt is still logged.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 646px; height: 1px; padding-top: 358px; margin-left: 745px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Reported here — the verdict lands in the logs and in the final chunk, so you can alert on it and tune the policy. What it cannot do is unsend the answer.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 425px; margin-left: 3px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 672px; height: 1px; padding-top: 455px; margin-left: 17px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
• Turn streaming on with stream: true in the request body. Supported on /chat/completions, /completions, /embeddings, and /messages.
• See the guardrail verdicts by sending x-portkey-strict-open-ai-compliance: false. The header defaults to true, and on that default the hook_results chunks are never emitted.
• Make the input guardrail enforce by setting async = false and deny = true on it. Left asynchronous, it logs a verdict and blocks nothing.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 425px; margin-left: 723px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #666666;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10.5px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #666666; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: nowrap;
display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 672px; height: 1px; padding-top: 455px; margin-left: 737px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;
div.span:
• Cost records as zero on every streamed call, because providers omit usage data by default. Send stream_options: {include_usage: true} or your budgets and chargeback reports will under-count streaming traffic.
• Request timeouts stop applying once one chunk has arrived in time. A provider that starts fast and then stalls will not trigger a 408.
• Output guardrails are not a control on streams. If a policy has to stop content reaching a user, it belongs on the input side, or the route has to be non-streaming.
